# Global instructions

## Writing

- Write short sentences in active voice.
- Use one instruction for each sentence.
- Do not use en dashes or em dashes. Use a comma, a colon, or a plain hyphen.

## Tools

- Use `uv run` for Python. Do not use pip.
- Do not delete files. Move them to the Trash.

## Tests

- Prefer end-to-end tests. Do not write unit tests after the code.
- At the end of an end-to-end test, keep a repeatable artifact as proof.

## Skills

- Before you write prose, apply the `@~/.claude/skills/unslop/SKILL.md` rules. This is a code span, not an import.

# Project instructions

Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) first. It names the files to read for each task.

No tests in this project. Do not write, run, or keep tests. Prove work with a real run on the data.

# Method

Checked against executable source and saved aggregate output on 2026-09-26.
This describes the local prepared website data. It does not establish the deployed site's state.

## Meaning and denominators

The map shows labels assigned to reviewer name records at selected Google Maps places.
The reviewed place determines the area. The reviewer's home does not.
Names do not establish ethnicity, nationality, residence, or culture.
Reviewers can include visitors and repeated records.

Area shares use retained classified records after the repeat cap and initial small-cell pooling.
Unknown and ambiguous records do not enter this denominator. Retained Other counts do.
City shares combine published area counts, then divide by their total.
Low-data areas supply no breakdown counts. This is not a mean of district percentages.
Country and region shares combine published counts from covered cities only.
These figures do not measure the resident population.

groups.ts defines the headline and group rows.
copy.ts combines city counts.
cities.ts combines country and region counts.

The headline excludes local, Western, Eastern European, and Other groups.
Anglo labels enter Western. The Middle Eastern display group includes North African labels.
Country codes in profile rows are display keys, not inferred citizenship.
For example, CO represents the Latin American group.
Group shares are rounded to one decimal. Headlines are rounded to whole percentages.
The display can hide a folded group with fewer than five counts.

One rule applies at every level: area, city, region, country, and the Europe overview.
Other stays in the denominator and never enters the headline numerator (changed 2026-10-18).
The enlarged home bars also change visual widths. Their labels retain the actual shares.
The main map uses a non-linear colour scale, with a maximum colour at 30% or more.

## Collection

[run_city.py](steps/run_city.py) controls current city steps.
city_config.py loads city inputs and search categories.
gen_queries.py builds business searches.

# Comparison pages

URL `/compare/<a>-vs-<b>/`. Composer `frontend/src/pseo/composers/compare.ts`. 26 pages are live: city pairs in Spain, Germany, and France.

## Current state (2026-10-18)

- Each page has a verdict, a dumbbell chart, top-5 tables, and a share row.
- The dumbbell label is cut at the right edge on desktop (seen 2026-10-07).
- Demand evidence for comparisons is sparse.

## Decisions

| Date | Decision | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-26 | Plan comparisons only where both cities have good coverage. | Avoid thin pages. | first-iteration/seo/07-comparisons/README.md |
| 2026-10-18 | Grow to about 150 pairs in phase 2: same-country big cities and capital pairs. Fix the cut label in the same package. | Modest growth with the demand evidence we have. | second-iteration/plan.md, package C2 |

## Open

- Check search demand for pairs before phase 2. Notes: [comparison demand](compare-demand.md).

# Direction

IndoEuroMap shows how multicultural each European city and neighbourhood is, with our own data.

## Who it is for

- People who want to know how multicultural their city or district is, and how it compares.
- Journalists, researchers, and city staff who need neighbourhood numbers across countries.

## What we promise

- One method for all of Europe. One source of truth: IndoEuroMap data.
- Numbers for each neighbourhood, city, region, and country.
- Clear limits on one methodology page.

## The second iteration: 18 October to 13 December 2026

| Goal | Today (18 October) | Target (13 December) |
|---|---|---|
| Direction | Plans in six folders, a 57 KB journal | One plan, one decision file per section, a status file under 60 lines |
| Traffic | 110 search clicks per 30 days, 0 referring domains | 300 search clicks per 30 days, 10 referring domains, 16 TikTok posts |
| Coverage | 641 live cities | 900 or more live cities, all cities above 50,000 people queued, buildserver does the work |

## What we do not do in this iteration

- No new SEO framework. No URL change. No title or H1 change before the 3 November reading.
- No method research. One classifier fix only. It gives data version 2.
- No money work. The report page and the research page stay as they are.
- No Instagram. No browser automation on any social account.
- No new tool layer. No knowledge tree, no context system, no session journal.
- No tests. A real run proves each change.

## Where things live

- [plan.md](plan.md): the work, in order, with proof for each package.
- [metrics.md](metrics.md): the weekly numbers and the reading dates.
- [status.md](status.md): the current state. 60 lines maximum. Replace it, do not append.
- [decisions/](decisions/index.md): one file per section of the site and per process.
- [../first-iteration/](../first-iteration/README.md): the archive. Read it only when a decision file points there.
